title: Essential technical tips for STAP cell conversion culture from somatic cells
protocol: Excise spleens from 1-week-old Oct4-gfp mice.
Mince the excised spleens using scissors.
Mechanically dissociate minced spleen tissue using a Pasteur pipette.
Dissolve adherent cells into single cells either mechanically or enzymatically.
Suspend dissociated spleen cells in PBS.
Strain suspended cells through a cell strainer.
Centrifuge cells at 1,000 rpm for 5 minutes.
Re-suspend collected cells in DMEM medium.
Add an equal volume of lympholyte to the re-suspended cells.
Centrifuge the mixture at 1,000 g for 20 minutes.
Remove red blood cells by suspending cell pellet in 1.8 ml of H2O.
Incubate suspension for 30 seconds.
Add 0.2 ml of 10× PBS to the suspended cells.
Add 3 ml of 1× PBS to the mixture.
Strain the cell suspension through a cell strainer.
Isolate the lymphocyte layer from the centrifuged sample.
Stain isolated lymphocytes with CD45 antibody.
Sort CD45+ cells by FACS Aria.
Treat 1 × 10^6 CD45+ cells with 500 μl of low-pH HBSS solution (pH 5.7) for 25 minutes at 37°C.
Centrifuge treated cells at 1,000 rpm at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Suspend the cell pellet with 494 µl of HBSS pre-chilled at 4°C.
Add 6 µl of diluted HCl (10 µl of 35% HCl in 590 µl of HBSS) to adjust pH to a final pH of 5.7.
Confirm the final pH in a pilot experiment and optimize the volume of HCl added as necessary.
Alternatively, suspend the cell pellet in HBSS-pH 5.4 pre-chilled at 4°C.
Incubate the cells suspended in HBSS in a CO2 incubator.
Shorten the incubation period with low-pH HBSS solution to 15 min if massive cell death occurs at one day after plating.
Remove the supernatant (low-pH solution) and re-suspend precipitated cells.
Plate the re-suspended cells onto non-adhesive culture plates typically at a density of 1×10^5 cells/ml in DMEM/F12 medium supplemented with 1,000 U LIF and 2% B27.
Maintain cell density at 1×10^5 to 1×10^6 cells per cm² of culture surface.
Check B27 quality by N2B27-2iLIF culture of ES cells before use.
Use donor mice that are 1 week old or younger for reprogramming efficiency.
STAP cell clusters are derived from multiple cells, not monoclonal cells.
Add LIF during days 2 to 7 for generating Oct3/4-GFP+ STAP cell clusters on day 7.
Transfer STAP cell clusters to ACTH-containing medium on MEF feeder cells.
Isolate and dissect STAP cell cluster into small pieces for seeding in ACTH medium.
Subject cells to a first passage using a conventional trypsin method after 4–7 days of culture.
Plate suspended cells in ESC maintenance medium containing 20% FBS for further culturing.
Transfer STAP cell clusters to Fgf4-containing trophoblast stem-cell medium on MEF feeder cells in 96-well plates.
Monitor colonies for growth in 96-well plates over time.
Observe changes in cell morphology as cells proliferate.
Subject the cells to the first passage during days 7-10 using a conventional trypsin method.
Perform subsequent passages at a split ratio of 1:4 every third day before the cells reach subconfluency.
Ensure that the cells are not completely dissociated; partial dissociation is optimal for maintaining viability and self-renewal.
